Background Inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenges affect respiratory muscle endurance in healthy individuals, which is considered to be an interleukin 6 (IL-6)–dependent mechanism. Whether nonpharmacological thermal therapies promote the endurance of loaded inspiratory muscles in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is unclear. The objectives of this study were to compare the effects of two thermal interventions on endurance time (ET) and plasma IL-6 concentration following an IRB challenge. Methods This study was a randomized, parallel-group, unblinded clinical trial in a single-center setting. Forty-two patients (aged 42–76 years) suffering from mild to severe COPD participated in this study. Both groups completed 12 sessions of the mud bath therapy (MBT) (n=22) or leisure thermal activity (LTA) (n=19) in a thermal spa center in Italy. Pre- and postintervention spirometry, maximum inspiratory pressure, and plasma mediators were obtained and ET and endurance oxygen expenditure (VO 2Endur ) were measured following IRB challenge at 40% of maximum inspiratory pressure. Results There was no difference in ΔIL-6 between the intervention groups. But, IRB challenge increased cytokine IL-6 plasma levels systematically. The effect size was small. A statistically significant treatment by IRB challenge effect existed in ET, which significantly increased in the MBT group ( P =0.003). In analysis of covariance treatment by IRB challenge analysis with LnVO 2Endur as the dependent variable, ΔIL-6 after intervention predicted LnVO2Endur in the MBT group, but not in the LTA group. Adverse events occurred in two individuals in the MBT group, but they were mainly transient. One patient in the LTA group dropped out. Conclusion MBT model improves ET upon a moderate IRB challenge, indicating the occurrence of a training effect. The LnVO 2Endur /ΔIL-6 suggests a physiologic adaptive mechanism in respiratory muscles of COPD patients allocated to treatment. Both thermal interventions are safe. Video abstract Keywords hydrotherapy cytokine IL-6 inspiratory resistive breathing balneotherapy pulmonary rehabilitation Introduction Countries rich in mineral water use different options of hydrotherapy (HT) as a traditional medicine approach to cure chronic diseases. Among the different effects of physical therapies with hypermineral thermal water, the antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of medicinal clays on skeletal muscles are acknowledged in several chronic diseases like osteoarthritis, 1 – 4 but not in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). In this condition, the clinical studies that have been undertaken to date have exclusively issued thermal water inhalations for treating upper and lower airway inflammation. 5 , 6 No study has considered thermal mud pack application as a method to increase the muscle temperature, in order to test its ability to affect the performance of loaded respiratory muscles in COPD. 7 Similar to a warm-up routine, thermal mud pack application might affect the performance of loaded inspiratory muscles via temperature-related mechanisms as well as nontemperature-related mechanisms, ie, via chemical and biochemical properties, which are achieved through the so-called maturation process of the thermal clay. 8 Consequently, there could be the potential for medicinal clays to impact the cytokine systemic response elicited from breathing against inspiratory resistive loads. Resistive breathing characterizes the course of many diseases of the respiratory system such as upper airway obstruction, bronchial asthma, and COPD exacerbations. 9 – 11 In addition, strenuous breathing against an added high inspiratory resistance, ie, intensive resistive breathing in healthy subjects, experimentally mimics the condition encountered in respiratory diseases. 12 Scientific evidence supports the role of inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) as an immunologic challenge. 12 , 13 Thus, IRB is here proposed as a test to challenge immunologic response of respiratory muscles in patients suffering from COPD while enduring at ≤50% of maximal inspiratory pressure. The clinical trial is aimed to evaluate whether the constituents of thermal treatments in Abano-Montegrotto Terme SPA (the natural clay from Costa and Lispida thermal lakes and Hyper thermal [sulfur-rich mineral] water from Colli Euganei mineral-water field [BIOCE]) can affect the endurance of respiratory muscles challenged against an inspiratory resistive load. We conducted this clinical trial with a parallel-group design in patients suffering from COPD (Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease [GOLD] stage I–III). We compared the mud (ie, medicinal clays) therapy (mud bath therapy [MBT]) model and the leisure thermal activity (LTA) model to test their efficacy in blunting the cytokine IL-6 plasma levels, circulating after a moderate IRB challenge. Further, we evaluated the effect of both thermal interventions on endurance time (ET), ie, the time to task failure. The cytokine IL-6 change and time of endurance upon IRB challenge are taken as the endpoint variables. Inspiratory time during IRB challenge ( T I_IRB ) and changes in endurance oxygen expenditure (VO 2_Endur ) upon the IRB challenge after thermal interventions were also explored to elucidate the homeostatic physiologic adaptations elicited in overloaded respiratory muscles by thermal interventions. Although performed at a submaximal inspiratory pressure in a stable phase of the disease, we hypothesized that the acute IRB challenge may constrain the freely adopted pattern of breathing in patients with chronic expiratory airflow obstruction. And, it may elicit upregulation of transcription with ensuing increase in cytokine plasma levels. If demonstrated, these effects would entail validating MBT model and LTA model as treatment options for individuals suffering from COPD and, in making passive warm-up routines a thermal and rehabilitative strategy to improve the endurance of inspiratory muscles.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the safety and efficacy of nonpharmacological thermal therapies, specifically Mud Bath Therapy (MBT) versus Leisure Thermal Activity (LTA), on the endurance of loaded inspiratory muscles and associated inflammatory/metabolic markers in patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). The aim was to compare their effects on endurance time (ET) and plasma IL-6 concentration following an inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge. The findings indicated that MBT significantly improved ET, suggesting a training effect and physiologic adaptive mechanisms in respiratory muscles. Both thermal interventions were found to be safe, as they did not significantly alter baseline IL-6, CRP, or ACTH levels. However, an IRB challenge systematically increased IL-6 levels in both groups, indicative of altered respiratory muscle glycogen utilization and a measurable inflammatory response.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Thermal therapy, including Mud Bath Therapy (MBT, also referred to as Mudpack Balneotherapy or medicinal clay applications as passive warm-up) and Leisure Thermal Activity (LTA).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Both MBT (n=22) and LTA (n=19) groups completed 12 sessions over 2 weeks. MBT involved daily mud pack application at 38-42°C for 20 minutes, followed by a thermal bath at 38°C for 8-15 minutes, and 60 minutes of bed rest, with optional access to thermal swimming pools once or twice daily for unsupervised leisure activities (each not exceeding 30 minutes). LTA consisted of 12 sessions over 2 weeks of unsupervised leisure activities (bathing, walking, swimming) in thermal swimming pools twice daily (each not exceeding 30 minutes). An inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge was performed at approximately 40% of maximal inspiratory pressure both pre- and post-intervention. No formal dose-response comparisons for the thermal therapies were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: IRB challenge systematically increased plasma IL-6 levels (P < 0.0005), with a small but statistically significant effect size, showing a timely rise (within 40 minutes) which was a 'milder and inconsistent increase' over baseline compared to healthy individuals. The coefficient of variation was five-folds higher in COPD patients (115% vs healthy 20%). However, thermal interventions (MBT or LTA) themselves did not significantly alter baseline IL-6 values either before or after application, and there was no significant difference in ΔIL-6 between MBT and LTA groups after IRB.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Mediates inflammation, immunologic challenge response, hormone-like glucose-regulatory mechanism, and signals critical low levels of glycogen content to working muscles.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During and after an inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge in COPD patients, both before and after thermal interventions (Mud Bath Therapy or Leisure Thermal Activity); also baseline levels with thermal interventions.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an immunologic response to inspiratory resistive breathing and altered respiratory muscle glycogen utilization (lower utilization or slower glycolysis activation). It predicts respiratory muscle metabolic adaptations and endurance oxygen expenditure in the MBT group, while its unchanged baseline levels confirm the safety of thermal interventions.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased in the Mud Bath Therapy (MBT) group (P=0.003) upon a moderate inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge, indicating a positive treatment effect. No significant change was reported for the Leisure Thermal Activity (LTA) group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects the capacity of inspiratory muscles to sustain work against a load, indicating muscle endurance.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Upon a moderate inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge following thermal interventions, particularly Mud Bath Therapy (MBT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates improved endurance and a training effect in the inspiratory muscles of COPD patients after MBT, signifying enhanced respiratory muscle performance.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged in average VO2, but predictive relationship observed
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: While average VO2 did not change, ΔIL-6 after intervention predicted LnVO2Endur in the Mud Bath Therapy (MBT) group, indicating a physiologic adaptive mechanism; no such prediction was observed in the Leisure Thermal Activity (LTA) group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects the metabolic cost of enduring an inspiratory resistive breathing challenge and is associated with homeostatic physiologic adaptations, specifically better oxygen utilization.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During an inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge after Mud Bath Therapy (MBT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests a physiologic adaptive mechanism in respiratory muscles of COPD patients allocated to MBT, indicating better oxygen utilization to cope with muscle's energy needs during sustained effort.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased after inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge as a metabolic consequence.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of anaerobic metabolism and metabolic efficiency of respiratory muscles, reflecting biochemical adaptations.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: After inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge and thermal interventions in COPD patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a training effect, stemming from metabolic consequences and biochemical adaptations in respiratory muscles, which contributes to increased endurance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Neither thermal treatment (MBT) nor leisure thermal activity (LTA) significantly modified the baseline values of CRP either before or after interventions.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Marker of systemic inflammation, mediating inflammatory responses.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Thermal interventions (Mud Bath Therapy/Leisure Thermal Activity) in COPD patients, both before and after application.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the safety of thermal interventions themselves, showing no significant inflammatory response induction at baseline.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No increase observed; the study was not able to measure any simultaneous HPA axis stimulation as assessed by an increase in IL-1β plasma levels following a moderated loaded breathing challenge.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cytokine that mediates inflammation and is involved in HPA axis stimulation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During and after a moderated inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge in COPD patients, both before and after thermal interventions (MBT/LTA).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Lack of increase indicates an absence of HPA axis stimulation under the tested conditions in COPD patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No specific changes or quantitative results reported for study interventions in this chunk.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Thermal interventions (MBT/LTA) and inspiratory resistance breathing (IRB) challenge in COPD patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammation; further data needed for specific effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No increase observed; the study was not able to measure any simultaneous HPA axis stimulation following a moderated loaded breathing challenge. Neither thermal treatment nor leisure thermal activity significantly modified baseline ACTH values, indicating consistent levels before and after interventions.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulates cortisol release and is a marker of hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis stimulation and sympatho-corticotrophic axis outflow, involved in stress response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During and after a moderated inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge in COPD patients, both before and after thermal interventions (MBT/LTA); also baseline levels with thermal interventions.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Lack of increase indicates an absence of HPA axis stimulation under the tested conditions, potentially due to moderate challenge intensity or impaired axis outflow, and also confirms the safety of thermal interventions themselves.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A cited study (Iranmanesh et al.) documented no increase in peak cortisol in response to cycling at both maximal and submaximal levels in COPD patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Involved in HPA axis stimulation and stress response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Responses to incremental bicycle ergometer in COPD patients (as reported by a cited study).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates failure to stimulate the HPA axis, possibly resulting from impaired sympatho-corticotrophic axis outflow in COPD patients.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A cited study (Iranmanesh et al.) documented no increase in peak epinephrine in response to cycling at both maximal and submaximal levels in COPD patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Involved in HPA axis stimulation, sympatho-corticotrophic axis outflow, and stress response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Responses to incremental bicycle ergometer in COPD patients (as reported by a cited study).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates failure to stimulate the HPA axis, possibly resulting from impaired sympatho-corticotrophic axis outflow in COPD patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Derived from respiratory oxygen expenditure (VO2Endur) and plasma IL-6 change (ΔIL-6 IRB)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: ANCOVA analysis indicated that higher VO2Endur in patients allocated to the Mud Bath Therapy (MBT) model is predicted by ΔIL-6 IRB when adjusting for baseline respiratory oxygen cost.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During an inspiratory resistive breathing (IRB) challenge, after exposure to the high temperature of medicinal clay packs.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a clinical biomarker of respiratory–metabolic adaptations. Higher oxygen expenditure during endurance, alongside increased Endurance Time (ET) without a change in average VO2, suggests better oxygen utilization to cope with muscle's energy needs.
